children: traded higher in the premarket on Tuesday after the company announced a late-stage trial win for dazodalibep, its experimental therapy for an autoimmune condition called Sjögren's disease.

said its Phase 3 OASIZ 301 study for dazodalibep met its primary endpoint, showing a statistically significant and clinically meaningful improvement in ESSDAI, a clinical tool that assesses systemic disease activity in Sjögren's.
The 48-week study enrolled more than 600 patients with Sjögren's disease and moderate-to-severe systemic disease activity.
The California-based pharma giant said improvements in ESSDAI appeared as early as Week 4 and added that it plans to disclose detailed data from OASIZ 301 at a future medical event.
As for safety, nasopharyngitis and urinary tract infections were among the most common adverse events, and discontinuations due to adverse events were low and balanced across treatment groups.
Despite being the second most common autoimmune rheumatic condition, Sjögren's disease has no FDA-approved therapies. Amgen
